segments.name: U.S. Retail
segments.description: Operates thrift stores in the United States, selling low-priced secondhand clothing, home goods and books to local retail customers.
segments.evidence: The increase in U.S. Retail segment profit primarily reflects higher profit from our comparable stores, partially offset by the impact of new stores.

segments.name: Canada Retail
segments.description: Operates thrift stores in Canada, selling low-priced secondhand clothing, home goods and books to local retail customers.
segments.evidence: The decrease in Canada Retail segment profit primarily reflects deleverage of expenses as a percentage of net sales on comparable store sales and the unfavorable impact of foreign currency exchange rates.

revenueModel.text: Retail customers pay for low-priced secondhand merchandise in stores, while wholesale customers pay for items unsuited for or unsold at retail.
revenueModel.evidence: Items that are unsuited for or unsold at retail stores are marketed to wholesale customers who reuse or repurpose the items they purchase from us.
